source.title: OSINT: WiFi Broadcast Packets Expose Your Home Address! + My Solutions + MAC Address Maps
source.description: Showing how your phone/computer's WiFi broadcast packets translate to your full home/house address (of the device) using passive sniffing (SIGINT) and public available data (OSINT). I talk about a quick misdirection solution I came up with for subscribers and talk about mac/network mapping. I run through Wipri and talk about coming feature. TIMESTAMPS: 1st: Intro 0:27 I begin to layout the problem for user privacy/explain/show packets 1:00 how this can lead to direct tracking 1:18 user app Wigle uploads mac addresses/networks to public map 2:10 How our device packets are collected legally/passively by anyone at all interested 2:56 Best general technique to enhance privacy and my idea/solution to this problem 4:10 problem/solution summary 4:55 How Wigle works (user app wardriving) 5:20 On ways to support the cause/channel/info on privacy routers 5:52 Importance of liking, sharing, subscribing w/notifications (hint: helps algorithm) 6:27 Misdirection and the 'whole picture' for its use in privacy 8:10 WiPri overview and explaining how each setting works to promote privacy 13:11 Main points to take home and overall summary/conclusion WiPri repository/code: https://gitlab.com/Aresesi/wipri To Download/Install WiPri using git command: git clone https://gitlab.com/Aresesi/wipri cd wipri Then simply run install.sh with root privileges (root needed to automatically install wipri directory to /etc/wipri for OUI/configuration and as a new command (install.sh gives you option to instal…

editorial.why_selected: Shows how the Wi-Fi network names your devices broadcast can be mapped back to a home address, then what you can do about it.
learning_outcomes: How Wi-Fi probe requests and public Wi-Fi maps leak location
Practical settings that reduce the leak
editorial.try_next: Look up your own router's network name on a public Wi-Fi map to see whether it's listed.
editorial.context_note: Dual-use: the same technique can locate other people. Shown here for self-defense.
